sections.text:
1: 001.05.1 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: The air flow will be provided by a pneumatically controlled piston system
This system shall provide:
01. Control of the rate of piston movement
02. Fluid path and solenoids to route vacuum from MSG vacuum connection plus pressure from MSG GN2
03. Pressure transducers to monitor pressure differential
04. Mounting for mass flow controller, fluid path, and transducer | 5: The flow rate is determined by the speed of the piston in the Aging Chamber.  The piston is moved pneumatically by a pressure differential driven by vacuum (aging chamber fill) or GN2 (aging chamber purge).  A software algorithm will determine and control the speed of the piston using data from a mass flow controller and a pressure transducer.
System assembly and successful pyrolysis precludes inlet leaking.  All ports must be sealed. Test procedure will include inspection for leaks. | 6: T | 8: X | 12: X | 13: X

sections.text:
1: 130.04.01 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.1 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Safety Critical and Fracture Critical Structures
All structural elements including associated interfaces, fasteners, and welds in the primary load path are considered Safety Critical Structures (SCS) and shall be analyzed per the guidelines of NASA-STD-5003 and SSP 52005.   | 5: Fracture Critical components are a subset of SCS and are defined as ones whose failure would present catastrophic hazards, i.e. they are not fail-safe. Through analysis SAME has determined that there are no Fracture Critical Components as part of the payload.  | 6: A | 17: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 437
sections.text:
1: 130.04.02 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.2 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Structural Loads
SAME will demonstrate compliance with structural loads requirements by conducting the appropriate inspections, analyses, and/or tests. Flight hardware will be designed to maintain structural integrity and functionality during all phases of the expected life cycle.  Verification of the structures and systems will consider static and dynamic loads encountered during assembly, testing, transportation, launch, ascent, space operations, descent and landing. NASA-STD-5002 will be utilized for defining methodologies, practices and requirements for conducting load analyses in the verification plan. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 438
sections.text:
1: 130.04.03 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.3 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Factors of Safety
NASA-STD-5001 and SSP 52005 will be used to establish design and test factors, as well as service life factors, to be used for flight hardware development and verification. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 439
sections.text:
1: 130.04.04 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.4 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Margins of Safety
All structural elements that are critical for safety and mission assurance shall be shown by analysis to have positive margins of safety.  The minimum margins of safety for all credible failure modes shall be determined. | 6: A | 17: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 440
sections.text:
1: 130.04.05 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.5 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Fracture Control
SAME does not have any fracture critical hardware.  However, if that determination is changed SAME will follow the guidelines in SSP-52005, and a Fracture Control Program will be implemented to meet the requirements of NASA-STD-5003 and SSP 30558. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 441
sections.text:
1: 130.04.07 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.7 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Strength Testing
The SAME Project will verify structural integrity by analysis alone without strength testing using the criteria and design factors specified in SSP 52005. Criteria and rationale will be reviewed and approved by the Payload Carrier/Integrator. For payloads launched on the Space Shuttle such as SAME, the Space Shuttle Payload Safety Review Panel will approve these criteria. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 442
sections.text:
1: 130.04.08.a | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.8 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Vibroacoustics
All SAME flight hardware will be flown in a stowed configuration, packed in foam.  SAME will use a combination of random and sinusoidal vibration testing (Protoflight vibration) to demonstrate the ability of the system to withstand launch requirements. | 5: See table in SAME-PLN-003, Section 3.4.8 for major system components and their vibration testing levels. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 443
sections.text:
1: 130.04.08.b | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.4.8 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Vibroacoustics
For a Class D experiment such as SAME, the workmanship vibration testing is a guideline.  Vibration sensitive components, such as optical components or particle sensors, and irreplaceable mission critical parts will see qualification program levels of vibration testing while in the “soft” stowage configuration that they will see for launch.   | 5: See table in SAME-PLN-003, Section 3.4.8 for major system components and their vibration testing levels. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 444
sections.text:
1: 130.04.08.c | 2: SAME-PLN-003

The custom boards that are part of the SAME experiment will be subjected to a workmanship level of testing.  The remaining electronics boards will only be tested as a part of the final assembly (during the final, protoflight vibe).  This testing will be performed to reveal inadequacies in workmanship.   | 5: See table in SAME-PLN-003, Section 3.4.8 for major system components and their vibration testing levels. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 445
sections.text:

This SLA material mockup will be tested without plating in order to characterize the worst case behavior of the raw material, and to allow more complete post vibration inspection.  | 5: See table in SAME-PLN-003, Section 3.4.8 for major system components and their vibration testing levels. | 6: NVR

For risk mitigation, subassemblies suspected of emissions and susceptibilities will be tested at the box level.  ORU change-outs (P-Trak and the Commercial Diagnostics Enclosure) will be made during conducted emissions and radiated emissions only. | 6: NVR

sections.text:
1: 130.07 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.7 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Vacuum, Thermal, and Humidity Requirements
Thermal tests and/or analysis will demonstrate the system under consideration will:
a) Properly operate in the flight environment, specifically temperature.
b) Properly control the thermal environment of temperature sensitive items or levy that requirement on an integrator.
c) Survive the temperature and humidity conditions of transportation (e.g. truck, plane, and space vehicle), storage and pre and post conditions of the carrier.
These tests will also act as an environmental screening to stimulate latent defects to maximize infant mortality. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 456
sections.text:
1: 130.07.2 | 2: SAME-PLN-003

Testing will be performed per SARG Table 3.7.2-1.  Modifications to the number of thermal cycles and temperature range may be made based on carrier requirements and/or hardware requirements.  These adjustments will be pre-approved by GRC. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 457
sections.text:
1: 130.07.3.1 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.7.3.1 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Thermal Cycling
Only the electronic boards of the SAME system will be thermal cycled.  This will help ensure that problems with latent manufacturing defects are addressed.  This also includes the boards for the P-TRAK and DustTrak commercial units that are part of the payload.  The system will undergo functional test at the end of the thermal cycling test. | 5: See table in SAME-PLN-003, Section 3.7.3.1 for thermal cycling information.

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 458
sections.text:
1: 130.07.4 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.7.4 | 3: Mechanical/ Electrical Engineering | 4: Description of Applicable [Thermal] Analysis
The SAME project shall perform Thermal Analysis on all systems and identify the following:
a) Heat sources and their magnitude
b) Methods employed to dissipate the heat from the sources
c) List of operating temperature ranges of the components
d) Environmental conditions and design criteria
e) Assessment of the thermal design and identification of additional analysis needed.
f) Evaluation of the susceptibility to humidity extremes.
g) Identification of any special testing requirements or conditions.
This minimum analysis will be completed by PDR. | 6: A | 17: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 459
sections.text:
1: 130.08.1 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.8.1 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Burn-In Tests
Systems under test that contain electronic (EEE) parts shall be burned-in to stimulate infant mortality failures. A minimum of one hundred hours of failure-free operation is required for SAME components, subsystems or systems prior to hardware turnover. The one hundred hours includes operational time accumulated during any functional and environmental testing.  | 5: Burn-in will be accomplished and recorded by way of system testing.  Log books will contain operating times. | 6: A | 7: X | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 460
sections.text:
1: 130.08.2.a | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.8.2 | 3: Multiple | 4: Mission Simulation Test
Flight and flight spare hardware will be subjected to mission simulation testing to provide confidence for both nominal and off-nominal operations. The hardware will also be run for extended periods of time, in part or in whole, to gain confidence that subsystems and functionality are sufficiently robust to meet the design goals. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 461
sections.text:
1: 130.08.2.b | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.8.2 | 3: Multiple | 4: Mission Simulation Test
Flight hardware shall complete an operational test, which exercises all equipment and software commands. A test plan for the scope and duration of this test shall be coordinated with the Principal Investigators and/or Project Scientists to verify the correct experiment operations. | 6: T | 7: X | 11: X | 13: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 462
sections.text:
1: 130.08.3 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
3.8.3 | 3: Multiple | 4: End-to-End Compatibility Test
An end-to-end compatibility test shall be conducted on the complete operational system in the final mission configuration, as closely as possible. This test would include the flight system; the flight operational software, the Carrier/carrier simulator, and the mission operations system, including the ground processing equipment and software in order to fully demonstrate operational compatibility and the ability of the entire system to perform as required during the mission.   | 5: The SAME project will develop a joint test plan with the MSG facility to define end-to-end interface tests with the MSG Ground Integration Unit (GIU).  | 6: T | 7: X | 11: X | 13: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 463
sections.text:

The SAME Project Office (PO) shall conduct appropriate safety analyses both at the system and subsystem levels.  Each system and subsystem shall be evaluated to determine the applicability of each technical safety requirement.  | 5: SAME will implement a system safety program that will assure the identification and control of hazards during design, fabrication, test, transportation, ground operations, launch, and retrieval. The SAME system safety program will be tailored to meet carrier-specific requirements, as outlined in the SARG. SAME will also meet the interface and safety requirements for Microgravity Science Glovebox as required by the MSG Interface Control Document (ICD) for SAME and the SAME Flight Safety Data Package (SAME-SDP-002). | 6: A | 12: X | 13: X | 14: X

sections.text:

Per ZIN QMS procedure P10001 Inspection and Test Procedure, all mechanical parts shall be inspected prior to their assembly into flight systems or subsystems to ensure they are free of any debris, defect or other material or substance that would interfere with their function. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108 | 6: I | 7: X | 12: X | 14: X

sections.text:

sections.text:

sections.text:

SAME shall prepare the appropriate materials-related information, including a certification letter for the acceptance of flight payload materials that will support NASA/GRC’s material certification of the experiment hardware. sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 477
sections.text:
1: 160.02.1.1 | 2: SAME-PLN-003

The SAME project will finish all metallic parts, assemblies, and equipment, including spares to provide protection from corrosion in accordance with the requirements of MSFC-SPEC-250. sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 478
sections.text:

The project will design with materials that meet the flammability requirements of NSTS 1700.7B, section 209.2. “The minimum use of flammable materials will be the preferred means of hazard reduction.” | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 479
sections.text:

Electrical wire insulation will be made of Teflon-based materials and meet the requirements of JSC 29353.  The M&P representative will be contacted regarding utilization of any wires or cables that do not meet of these specifications. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 480
sections.text:

6.2.1.4 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Flammability (Applicable to All Vehicle Areas)
Electrical wiring cable ties shall be made from ECTFE (Halar) material to provide an efficient means of hazard reduction. This is in preference to expending resources on verifying the spacing of flammable cable tie materials allowed by JSC 29353. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108 | 6: I | 17: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 481
sections.text:
1: 160.02.1.5 | 2: SAME-PLN-003

All materials shall meet the fluid systems compatibility requirements of NSTS 1700.7B, paragraph 209.1.  NASA-STD-6001, Test 15 "Reactivity of Materials in Aerospace Fluids," shall be performed to evaluate any changes resulting from exposure of a material to an aerospace fluid that makes the fluid or material unusable. When materials can be exposed to hazardous fluids by a credible single barrier failure, an engineering evaluation and analysis of test data will be conducted to demonstrate the acceptability of the configuration. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-202

sections.text:

Off gas testing will be performed on the flight hardware at MSFC during shipment to KSC. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 483
sections.text:
1: 170.01.a | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.1 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Reliability, Availability & Maintainability - General Requirements
SAME will plan and implement a reliability program that interacts effectively with other program disciplines, including systems engineering, hardware design, and product assurance.  The preferred development approach is to develop prototype hardware/software to provide the final flight design for experiment hardware/software. The reliability effort will be conducted throughout the design process, to the final design of the flight hardware.  Much of the reliability will be demonstrated through component and assembly testing.  Reliability and availability analyses will be performed concurrently with design to indicate areas of risk, promote design improvements, and increase system reliability and supportability.  | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 484
sections.text:
1: 170.01.b | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.1 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Reliability, Availability & Maintainability - General Requirements
All non-conformances that occur during build-up or testing of flight hardware shall be reported and tracked to completion per the ZIN-Tech Quality Management System (QMS). | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108 | 6: A | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 485
sections.text:
1: 170.02.1.a | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.1 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Reliability Allocation and Prediction Analysis
The SAME project shall perform a low-fidelity reliability prediction and failure mode analysis. The system level reliability for the mission duration and duty cycle will be improved to the greatest extent possible with a combination of highly reliable components and flight spares complemented with alternate (off-nominal) procedures. | 6: A | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 486
sections.text:
1: 170.02.1.b | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.1 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Reliability Allocation and Prediction Analysis
When using a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) component, SAME will procure the optimal reliability component. The selection will be based on the following:
1) Acceptable vendor screening program to the project requirements (burn-in, thermal cycle and vibration levels)
2) Acceptable vendor quality control program
3) A Mean-Time Between Failure (MTBF) which yields a reliability of 90% or greater for the expected life cycle of the component, whenever this data and these parts are available from the vendor
4) Radiation hardness and minimized EMI susceptibility, as needed | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 487
sections.text:
1: 170.02.2 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.2 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Burn-In Periods
The SAME project shall provide a statement of the burn-in periods (both total burn-in and failure free) that will be required for all equipment prior to delivery, and how the periods relate to the overall equipment life. | 5: Experiment run times will be provided (log books.) | 6: A | 7: X | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 488
sections.text:
1: 170.02.3 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.3 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Failure Modes and Effects Analysis and Critical Items List
The SAME project will perform a Failure Analysis, performed on the major assembly/component level in order to determine the criticality of its internal hardware devices, relative to mission success and safety. Critical items are those components or subassemblies whose failure modes are safety critical or mission-success critical. In those instances where critical failure modes cannot be designed out of the intended system, the hardware will be designed for minimum risk or a spare component will be flown. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 489
sections.text:
1: 170.02.4 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.4 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Single Point Failure List
There are no single point failures for loss of life or vehicle in the SAME Experiment.  Any single point failures that could result in injury, loss of life, vehicle, or science mission, will be determined from the Hazards Analysis and the FMEA.  Single point failures that would compromise mission success will be determined and documented as a result of the FMEA and will become part of the SAME risk list to be accepted with rationale, watched, or mitigated as they are evaluated. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 490
sections.text:
1: 170.02.5 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.5 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Failure Detection
SAME shall provide a description of the automatic or manual failure detection, isolation and recovery methods supported by the design under analysis. | 5: Will be contained in crew procedures as malfunction procedures. | 6: A | 18: X | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 491
sections.text:
1: 170.02.8 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.8 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Worst Case Analysis
Worst-case analysis will be performed by the project on all circuits that support safety critical functions.  The most sensitive design parameters, including those that are subject to variations that could degrade performance, will be included in the analysis. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 492
sections.text:
1: 170.02.9 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.2.9 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Trend Analysis
The project will assess component, subsystem and system reliability and safety risk by identifying variables through testing and non-conformance reports. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 493
sections.text:
1: 170.03.2 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.3.2 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Sparing and Logistics Planning
The SAME project will build and maintain spare subsystem components as required by the customer.  The spare unit will be composed of flight parts and will be identical to the flight unit.  The Fit/Functional Model hardware is intended to be composed of some flight-like parts and procedures. This unit may be available for sparing of some parts or subsystems.  Information and support will be provided to the Project Manager for sparing and logistics planning. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 494
sections.text:
1: 170.04.1 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.4.1 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Maintainability Allocation and Prediction Analysis
The project shall perform a maintainability allocation and prediction assessment.  Spare hardware will be flown, as mass allocations allow, where failures are likely and unavoidable.  Procedures shall be developed to troubleshoot, fix, or work around malfunctions. | 6: A | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 495
sections.text:
1: 170.04.2 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.4.2 | 3: QA / Multiple | 4: Limited Life Items
Limited storage life items have a specified storage time limit (shelf-life), which is less its planned storage time. Examples of limited storage-life items are solid chemicals, chemical mixtures and/or solutions, solvents, lubricants, epoxies, or even hardware devices.  The project controls limited storage-life items by the expiration date indicated on any limited storage-life item. Whether dated by the manufacturer or by the project at receiving/creation, any expiration date is checked before use and recorded in the process plan or log book. For safety critical operations, this is validated by a QA sign-off. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 496
sections.text:
1: 170.04.3 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.4.3 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Qualitative Maintainability Analysis
The Project shall perform qualitative maintainability analysis to assure that the system is maintainable and that there is an effective maintenance capability to restore functions to their full capacity throughout the intended operational life of the system. The following maintenance design features are required: See SAME-PLN-003 for list of design features. | 6: A | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 497
sections.text:
1: 170.04.4 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
7.4.4 | 3: Multiple | 4: Provisions For Failure Detection
SAME has provisions for failure detection, annunciation, and recovery processes which include manual control of the automated processes.  When functionality is restored it is confirmed.  There are no catastrophic or critical hazards which require failure detection. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 498
sections.text:
1: 180.02 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.2 | 3: QA | 4: Quality Assurance Requirements - General Requirements
SAME will maintain an effective and timely Quality Assurance (QA) Program, which assures that quality requirements are met through control of design, operations, processes, procedures, testing, and inspection. The SAME Quality Assurance Program utilizes and is governed by the ZIN Technologies, Inc. Quality Management System (QMS), which is ISO 9001 certified. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 499
sections.text:
1: 180.04.a | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.4 | 3: CM | 4: Configuration Management and Verification
All documents, drawings and revisions, which define and verify the system, shall be kept under configuration control. The SAME Configuration Management Plan (SAME-PLN-002) specifies responsibilities and addresses the following: See SAME-PLN-003 for more details. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108 | 6: I | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 500
sections.text:
1: 180.04.b | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.4 | 3: CM | 4: Configuration Management and Verification
The System configuration items shall be placed under configuration control and base-lined at the earliest possible time.  This may be at the fit/functional, qual or flight model stage, but in all cases, the system shall be baselined by CDR. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108 | 6: I | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 501
sections.text:
1: 180.04.c | 2: SAME-PLN-003

The responsible project configuration control personnel shall assure that documents are kept current, and when changes are made, they are made promptly and include changes to all associated documentation and the system. The Configuration Management Plan shall assure that only the latest drawings, including all changes, are used for the fabrication, assembly, testing and inspection of all components. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108 | 6: I | 17: X | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 502
sections.text:
1: 180.07.2 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.7.2 | 3: QA | 4: Training for Personnel
As required by the applicable standards, only individuals qualified and/or certified to perform these activities shall be permitted to perform the work and inspection of flight hardware.  This applies to assembling electrical cables, fiber optics cables, soldering, conformal coating and welding. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108

Zin's Quality System | 6: I | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 503
sections.text:
1: 180.07.4 | 2: SAME-PLN-003

The SAME Project shall maintain a controlled bonded storage area, which is capable of storing flight material, parts and assemblies. The level and type of environmental control shall be defined based on the specifics of the flight material, parts and assemblies being stored. The environmental control shall minimally protect the flight items from excessive temperatures and humidity, and from contamination. Electrostatic discharge (ESD) control shall be implemented for ESD sensitive parts as defined in Section 8.8. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108

Zin's Quality System | 6: I | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 504
sections.text:
1: 180.07.5 | 2: SAME-PLN-003

The logbooks shall document all actions taken on the component, and shall provide for easily accessible total operating time of the component under control. | 5: Deleted by SAME-ECO-108

Zin's Quality System | 6: I | 19: X

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 505
sections.text:
1: 180.08.1 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.8.1 | 3: QA | 4: Contamination Control Plan
The SAME Project will use W09010 Contamination Control and Cleanliness Requirements as its contamination control plan. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 506
sections.text:
1: 180.09 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.9 | 3: QA | 4: Electrostatic Discharge Prevention

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 507
sections.text:
1: 180.10 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.10 | 3: QA | 4: Nonconformance and Problem Reporting and Control
SAME will operate a closed-loop nonconformance control system for failures and discrepancies and provide documentation of each nonconformance per the ZIN P13001 Procedure for the Control of Nonconforming Product.  In this process ZIN F13001 Nonconformance Report is initiated.  ZIN Quality monitors the disposition of the Nonconformance.  The non-conformance is reviewed and closed-out by the responsible engineer, ZIN quality assurance, the SAME project task lead, and SAME Project Manager.  This procedure also levees requirements for waivers and deviations based on the disposition of the non-conformance. | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 508
sections.text:
1: 180.12 | 2: SAME-PLN-003 
8.12 | 3: Systems Engineering | 4: Inspection and Test of Stored Limited-Life Hardware
In the event that limited-life hardware items are stored or stocked, a test plan or line-item on a Process Plan will be developed which assures that limited-life items have not been degraded or damaged during storage. The plan will address proper handling, including environmental conditions, to mitigate damage or prolong life, and testing to assure the stored items meet required specifications. Limited-life items not meeting the requirements set forth in the plan will be considered nonconforming, and handled in accordance with paragraph 8.9. Limited life items will be identified on a list and a log of their remaining life maintained. (The definition and requirements for limited life items are shown in Section 7.4.2.) | 6: NVR

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 509
sections.text:

sections.text:
1: 311.1.a | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.1.1.1.a | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Load Requirements
Investigations will be designed to withstand the launch and landing conditions when stowed in the MPLM, Middeck or other transportation vehicles. For design consideration the Investigation will use the acceleration loads defined in Table I when stowed in the MPLM or Middeck. These loads are based on a worst case condition of the Middeck and MPLM. The IIT will provide the investigator with the acceleration and random vibration data of the carrier the investigation is manifested on. Additional requirements or data may be required depending on the configuration of the investigation and the requirements of the carrier.
It is assumed that the loads imposed by the random vibration environment on stowed items in foam can be neglected in design consideration. The Investigation will conduct a workmanship test, for instance on electrical components or mechanisms, based on the random vibration environment defined in Table I. The Investigation must ensure that the hardware will survive the workmanship random vibration level. | 6: NVR

The Investigation shall participate in a physical and integrated interface verification of the investigation hardware at least once during the development and integration process per the MSG Investigation Integration Plan, MSFC-PLAN-3052. The integrated test requires that the investigation test in its flight configuration and verify all interfaces with the MSG. Signal circuits with frequency components equal to or above four megahertz shall use controlled impedance transmission and reception media such as shielded twisted 72-ohm cable, "twin-ax" cable, "tri-ax" cable, or "co-ax" cable. "Tri-ax" cable shall use the center and inner shield conductors for unbalanced transmission, referenced to primary structure at a single point with the outer shield multipoint grounded as an "overshield". dc isolated, single-ended circuits coupled by coaxial cable with the shield terminated 360 degrees at each end and at available intermediate points, shall be permitted for signals with the lowest frequency component equal to or above 4 MHz. | 5: Disposition changed to N/A by SAME-ECO-229;

1: 324.2 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.2.4.2 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Electrical Bonding 
Investigation hardware connected to the RPDA power sources available in the WV shall be bonded in accordance with the following requirements. Electrical bonding is the process of providing good electrical connection across mechanical interfaces to minimize electrical potential differences between equipment and individual parts of structure. Good electrical bonding provides: Fault current paths for protection against fire and personnel shock, Provides a current path for radio frequencies for proper operation of filters and shields, and a means to prevent or safely discharge static charges.
Electrical bonds are classified according to the purpose for the bond. There may be more than one purpose for bonding a specific interface, and the bond shall meet the requirements of each applicable class. Notes shall be provided on assembly drawings indicating the applicable class or classes. The material used in the MSG work volume is 7075 aluminum nickel struck. A bonding test shall be performed during integrated testing with the Engineering Unit. | 5: Must test with EU, test results to be provided to IPIM. | 6: T & I & A | 8: X | 10: EL-020
EL-022 | 12: X | 13: X | 16: X* | 17: X

sections.text:
1: 324.2.1.1 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.2.4.2.1.1 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Class H Bonding (Shock and Fault Protection) 
Fault current, due to short circuits to equipment case or structure, may cause shock or fire hazards. All electrically conductive equipment cases that may develop potentials due to short circuits shall be electrically bonded to structure. The bond shall minimize shock hazard voltages and allow proper operation of circuit protection devices such as circuit breakers or fuses. Bonding of structural joints in the fault current return path shall provide for the maximum current that may be delivered by the power supply until the fuse or circuit breaker disconnects. For personnel and fire safety the fault current return path shall be capable of conducting a minimum of 500% overload current for a time period of 0.5 second. Typical personnel protection breakers will trip within 0.2 second after a hard short to case. Resultant voltage on the enclosure of the affected component must not exceed 4.5 volts, and no fire or damage to the bond is allowed. See MSFC-RQMT-2888 for more information. | 5: Must test with EU, test results to be provided to IPIM. | 6: T & I & A | 7: X | 8: X | 10: EL-020
EL-022 | 12: X | 13: X | 16: X* | 17: X

1: 324.2.1.2 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.2.4.2.1.2 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Class R Bonding
All electrical components which use or produce electromagnetic energy shall be installed to provide a continuous low impedance path from the equipment enclosure to the conductive structure.  The Investigation shall demonstrate by test or analysis that the proposed bonding method results in a dc resistance of less than 2.5 milliohms across each faying surface in the bond path from enclosure to structure and a total bond path impedance of less than 100 milliohms up to a frequency of 1 megahertz. Tests have shown that bonding joints that consist of direct metal-to-metal contact over a large area (greater than 1 square inch) of the mating surfaces meet the RF impedance requirement. The bond from the equipment enclosure to the mounting plate furnished with the equipment shall also comply with these requirements, except that a suitable flat ground strap may be used across any necessary vibration isolators or other environment isolators. 1: 324.2.4 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.2.4.2.4 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Methods of Bonding 
Equipment and structure with metal-to-metal joints that are joined by processes that transform the mated surfaces into one piece of metal, such as by welding or brazing, are considered permanent and inherently bonded.  Semi-permanent joints are held together by screws, rivets, clamps, etc.  Semi-permanent mating surfaces shall be cleaned of all insulating material before connection to provide a good electrical bond.  Clamping pressure across the joint shall be adequate to assure a secure mechanical connection. Fasteners or their threads shall not be used as primary bonding paths.
Self-tapping screws; zinc-plated bolts, nuts, or screws; star, anodized, or zinc-plated washers; or any cadmium-plated hardware shall not be used for bonding purposes. | 5: Must test with EU, test results to be provided to IPIM. | 6: T & I & A | 7: X | 8: X | 10: EL-020

sections.text:
1: 324.2.4.1.2 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.2.4.2.4.1.2 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Jumpers/Straps
Bond straps or jumpers may be used to meet Class “H” or “S” bonding requirements.  The usefulness of bond straps or jumpers for Class “R” bonds is very limited.  Straps for Class “R” bonds shall be used only as a last resort. Bonding straps installed across shock mounts or other suspension or support devices shall not impede the performance of the mounting device. They shall be capable of withstanding the anticipated motion and vibration requirements without suffering metal fatigue or other failure. Extra care should be utilized in the attachment of the ends of bonding straps to prevent arcing or other means of electrical noise generation with movements of the strap.  Bond straps or wires shall be sized to carry fault current. | 6: T & I & A | 7: X | 8: X | 10: EL-020

sections.text:
1: 324.3.1.1.1 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.2.4.3.1.1.1 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Frequency or Rise/Fall Time 
For Table IX, EMC Classification, Wire Type, and Shield Grounding classification purposes, the fundamental component of steady state operation will determine the frequency of the circuit unless the rise/fall time (pulsed wave forms) is less than 10 microseconds. If the rise/fall time is less than 10 microseconds and the voltage is less than 6 volts, the circuit shall be classified as Radio Frequency (RF) regardless of the fundamental frequency. Power circuits which are switched on and off will be classified as HO or EO even if their rise/fall times are less than 10 microseconds. | 6: NVR

sections.text:

3.2.4.3.1.1.2 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Impedance 
The actual impedance of the interconnecting circuit, i.e., the complex "Z" that includes resistance, inductance and capacitance, will be used to classify the source and load impedances using Table IX. These source and load impedances determine the magnetic and electric field coupling mode category. The equivalent circuit pickup resistance, i.e., the sum of the load and equivalent reactive/resistive components, will be used to identify potential areas for magnetic or electric field coupling. | 6: NVR

3.2.4.3.1.2.3.2 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Separation Requirements 
Each bundle type of one code will be physically separated from other bundles to meet the 20-dB isolation requirement of MSG IIRD Section 3.2.4.3.1.2. Metallic channel separation will be permitted in lieu of physical separation, provided that the channel separator height is no less than the largest cable bundle diameter requiring separation and that analysis shows that the channels provide the required 20-dB isolation. The application of such metallic barriers in lieu of physical separation will be identified on all wiring diagrams containing these circuits. Cable bundle placement in all wire trays will also be determined using minimum-to-maximum voltage or sensitivity requirements of Table IX, e.g., EO and RF cable bundles will have maximum separation in the placement of adjacent wire bundles. | 6: NVR

The length of the termination-to-ground lead for RF circuits shall be the minimum practical and shall not exceed 3 inches. 3.3.2 | 3: Software Engineering | 4: Investigation I/O Interface
The MSG provides 8 analog inputs, 8 discrete inputs, and 8 digital outputs, split equally between two connectors in the Work Volume. When properly configured and enabled, the Experiment Control Board (ECB) reads the input lines and transmits the data to the RC. The RC in turn transmits the data to the ISS via the Low Rate Data Link (LRDL) in a Low Rate Telemetry (LRT) packet. The digital output lines are controlled via commands to the RC. | 6: NVR

When the MLC is to be used outside the work volume, the Investigation may connect to either the J404 feed-through port in the front of the MSG WV, or the J706 connector located on the CMP or to the J312 connector located on the WV rear wall. In either case, the Investigation provided connector (P404, P706 or P312), shall be of type MS27467T9F35P, and shall be compatible with the connector and pin assignments identified in Table XXV.
The MSG provides two cables for use with MLC outside the work volume:
W201 - converts RS232 to RS422 signal levels (the converter is powered from the serial lines). This cable allows the MLC outside the work volume to communicate RS422 to an investigation inside the work volume. The investigation must provide a cable from the J404 or J312 connector to the experiment.
W205 - allows MLC outside the work volume to communicate RS232 to an investigation inside the work volume. The investigation must provide a cable from the J404 or J312 connector to the experiment. | 5: Disposition changed to A by SAME-ECO-229;

sections.locator: sheet VPERD matrix PLN-005 baseline, row 888
sections.text:
1: 341.1 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.4.1.1 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: WV Air Circulation System (ACS)
The WV air circulation is established by the MSG Air Handling Unit (AHU). The AHU heat exchanger provides 200 W of investigation cooling, at an airflow rate of 1200 l/min and a maximum velocity of 0.044 m/s at the centerline of the WV. The airflow can be varied between 15% and 100% depending on fan speed settings. The rate and velocity is calculated without an Investigation inside the WV. Investigation power draw data shall be used to determine if the AHU heat exchanger is capable of removing the dissipated heat load. The filtration system provides for particulate removal, filtration of single spillage (see section 3.7.3), and oxidation of CO to CO2 by means of a built-in catalyst. Due to the hydroscopic nature of the filters, the humidity inside the WV will be maintained at or below cabin level. Figure 26 provides block diagram of the MSG air loops. | 6: A | 10: FD-002 | 12: X | 13: X

1: 341.2.1.d | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.4.1.2.1.d | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Investigation Coldplate Mounting Requirements
Total heat dissipation to the coldplate shall be no more than 800 Watts. 
The predicted MSG coldplate temperatures are shown in Figure 27 and Figure 28.  
These predicted coldplate temperatures are based on a MSG Rack coolant inlet temperature of 18.3 C.  These temperatures are a function of experiment heat dissipation to the coldplate, experiment heat dissipation to Glovebox air, and coldplate coolant flow rate. Coolant flows to the MSG rack equipment, heat exchangers, and the MSG coldplate in series. 1: 374.3 | 2: MSFC-RQMT-2888 
3.7.4.3 | 3: Mechanical Engineering | 4: Chemical Releases
Investigations that use chemicals that would create a toxicity problem or cause a hazard to ISS or MSG hardware if released shall provide adequate containment.  Containment shall be provided by the use of a pressure vessel or the use of two or three redundantly sealed containers, depending on the toxicological hazard for a chemical with a vapor pressure below 15 psia. The Investigation must assure that each level of containment will not leak under the maximum use conditions (i.e. vibration, temperature, pressure, etc.). The release of methanol, ethanol, isopropyl alcohol, n-propyl alcohol, n-butyl alcohol, acetone, ethylene glycol, and propylene glycol into the ISS habitable environment shall be prohibited. The release of these compounds due to normal materials offgassing is exempt from this requirement. | 5: Closed when safety verification is closed. | 6: A & I (PSRP) | 8: X | 10: (Safety) | 12: X | 13: X | 19: X

Investigations shall use materials and parts that meet the materials requirements specified in NSTS 1700.7, ISS Addendum. This requirement also applies to all Commercial/Off the shelf (COTS) parts used in the investigation.

3.10.8.2 | 3: Electrical Engineering | 4: Mismatched
The design of electrical connectors shall make it impossible to inadvertently reverse a connection or mate the wrong connectors if a hazardous condition can be created. Payload and on-orbit support equipment, wire harnesses, and connectors shall be designed such that no blind connections or disconnections must be made during payload installation, operation, removal, or maintenance on orbit or during ground operations at KSC unless the design includes scoop proof connectors or other protective features. For payload equipment, for which mismating or cross-connection may damage ISS or MSG provided equipment, plugs, and receptacles (connectors), shall be selected and applied such that they cannot be mismatched or cross-connected in the intended system as well as adjacent systems. Although identification markings or labels are required, the use of identification alone is not sufficient to preclude mismating. rows: Smoke Generation Duct (Aging Chamber Inlet Elbow)
a) Configuration: Square or round duct with air flow through the duct.
The smoke generation duct shall be round with air flow through the duct.

b) Optical access: One view is required of the sample and the downstream flow. This view should be illuminated and imaged by a color video camera (visible light only).  The orientation of the light relative to the imager should permit the visualization of the light scattered by the smoke.

The duct has a port downstream of the sample, with a wide-angle camera mounted to view the sample and the first portion of the flow duct.  Lighting will provide image visibility in the closed tube and has been demonstrated in 1-g with sample smoke.

01. The duct shall have a port approximately 1 inch downstream of the sample.
02. Mounting shall be provided for the camera at the port.

Imaging Device Electrical
01. Power camera
02. Control camera
03. Record camera
04. Power LED's

01. Power to the camera is routed from the MSG Video + 12 VDC source.
02. Electronics will be provided to allow the DACU to control the camera.
03. Video signal is routed to a transcoder, then to the MSG monitor and recorder.
04. Power is supplied to the LED's
Reference SAME electrical schematic
#__________________
See # 008.01.2
Provide software to control (if necessary) and record the images from the camera and the LED's

The DACU shall have the ability to control MSG video drawer functions by sending video command packets to the SPLC.  The controllable video drawer functions are determined by the requirements of the video drawer command group, Section 4.4.5.
The DACU shall accept a set of commands to perform MSG video drawer operations.  The video drawer group commands shall perform the operations listed in Table 6 of SAME-DOC-004.
The DACU shall control power to any combination of the camera lights.
